title: Ravens QB Lamar Jackson expected to miss 6-10 weeks following thumb surgery
content:
Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson suffered a broken and dislocated right thumb against the Buffalo Bills two weeks ago, the team announced Friday morning. His recovery timeline after surgery will be six to 10 weeks, but it is unclear whether he will be able to return to the Ravens this season.

“Recovery timelines are challenging to predict, but injuries like this that require surgery typically take about 6-10 weeks to heal,” Ravens coach Jesse Minter said in a statement. “He is doing everything he can to get back, and we will let his progress guide the timing of his return.”

Jackson has already undergone the surgery and has started rehabbing.

Jackson suffered the injury on his first play of the team’s Week 8 game against the Bills. He was coming back from a three-week absence due to an ankle sprain he suffered against the Titans in Week 4.

Tyler “Snoop” Huntley suffered a turf toe injury in that same game against the Bills, and the Ravens were forced to turn to undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano for the remainder of that Buffalo loss, as well as the subsequent Thursday night game against Jacksonville.

The Ravens then finalized a trade for Cardinals quarterback Jacoby Brissett, sending a 2027 fifth-round pick to Arizona to acquire the veteran. Brissett will start for Baltimore on Monday against the Chargers.
